title: Breaking the Persona Link: Can a Single 'Honesty' System Prompt Block Emergent Misalignment at Inference?

original_idea.body:
# Can a Single Honesty System Prompt Block EM at Inference?

**Problem:** Whether a strong system-prompt intervention can suppress EM post hoc is under-studied.

**Direction:** On a released EM organism, measure misalignment under no prompt vs honesty/aligned-assertion/CoT-reflection prompts.

**Why it matters:** A cheap prompt mitigation if it works; a stronger warning if it doesn't.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2506.11618; arXiv:2506.11613; arXiv:2507.06253.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Either a cheap deployment-time mitigation or a stronger warning that EM is trained-in; defensible either way.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only system-prompt comparison on a released organism; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: a few system-prompt conditions, single EM eval, clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Released organisms, inference-only; weak lab incentive on this specific probe.

novelty.reasoning: Prompt-sensitivity of EM is noted; this specific inference-time suppression test may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: EM prompt-sensitivity noted; system-prompt suppression test may be open.
